* **Limit Background App Refresh:** Prevent apps from running and fetching data in the background (**Settings > General > Background App Refresh** on iPhone, or **Settings > Apps > [App Name] > Battery** on Android).

### 2. Adjust Display Settings
* **Lower screen brightness:** Set your brightness manually to a comfortable lower level, or enable auto-brightness.
* **Reduce auto-lock / screen timeout:** Set your screen to turn off after 30 seconds or 1 minute of inactivity.
* **Use Dark Mode:** If your phone has an OLED/AMOLED screen, using Dark Mode can save significant power because black pixels are turned off completely.

### 3. Manage Connectivity & Location Services
* **Disable unused radios:** Turn off Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or Personal Hotspot when you’re not actively using them.
* **Switch to Wi-Fi where possible:** Connecting to Wi-Fi typically uses less power than mobile data, especially in areas with poor cellular signal (where the phone boosts transmission power to search for signal).
* **Audit Location Services:** Go to your location settings and set apps to access location **"Only While Using"** rather than "Always." Turn off location entirely for apps that don't need it.

### 4. Optimize System & Notification Settings
* **Use Low Power Mode / Battery Saver:** Turn this on when your battery drops below 30–40% to automatically throttle background processes and lower display refresh rates.
* **Limit push notifications:** Every notification wakes up the screen and triggers network activity. Turn off notifications for apps that aren't essential.
* **Turn off haptic feedback / vibration:** Vibration motors consume noticeably more power than simple audio tones.

### 5. Check Battery Health & Charging Habits
* **Check battery health:** 
  * On iPhone: Go to **Settings > Battery > Battery Health & Charging**. If maximum capacity has dropped below 80%, the battery may need replacement.
  * On Android: Many phones show battery health in **Settings > Battery** or via manufacturer diagnostic tools (e.g., Samsung Members).
* **Avoid extreme temperatures:** Both intense heat (direct sunlight, charging in hot cars) and freezing cold can temporarily or permanently degrade battery performance.
* **Keep software updated:** Ensure your operating system is updated to the latest version, as updates often include power-management fixes.
